sources.citation: Wikibuku bahasa Indonesia contributors (Bennylin, 2020-03-30). 'Bahasa Towe' (section 'Di Provinsi Papua'). Indonesian Wikibooks; verbatim recopy of Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa, Peta Bahasa entry 'Bahasa Towe', Provinsi Papua.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Nothing. 743 bytes of wikitext: where the language is spoken, the neighbouring languages (Towe Hitam, Bias, Tefalma, Terfones, Towe Atas, Lules, Melki) and the dialectometry sentence 'isolek Towe merupakan sebuah bahasa dengan persentase perbedaan berkisar 96,75%--100%'. No phonology, no tekanan/nada/aksen.

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew & Harald Hammarström. 2018. The Trans New Guinea family. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide (The World of Linguistics 4), 21-195. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. doi:10.1515/9783110295252-002 (open-access chapter, OAPEN 20.500.12657/23719).
sources.note: For Towei nothing: the chapter classifies Towei's entire documentation as 'wordlist' (Galis 1956, Voorhoeve 1971, 1975, Wambaliau 2004) and calls the Pauwasi languages 'scantily documented'. Its phonology section (sec. 4, 'tonal and accent systems') surveys TNG tone/pitch accent/stress typology by region without mentioning any Pauwasi language. Useful as an authoritative 2018 confirmation that no phonological description of Towei exists.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald. 2010. The status of the least documented language families in the world. Language Documentation & Conservation 4: 177-212.
sources.note: Nothing; Towei [ttn] mentioned only regarding Pauwasi classification (p. 196).

sources.citation: Greenhill, Simon J. (ed.). TransNewGuinea.org: 'Language: Towei' (towe1240 / ttn), 36 lexical items after Voorhoeve (1975).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Nothing: 36 Voorhoeve 1975 checklist forms (e.g. kereser 'tooth', onggo 'I'), no stress marks (Voorhoeve's checklist states stress and pitch are not indicated), no prosodic note.

sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.6.2.2.13 'The Pauwasi Stock' (pp. 418-419): 'The only published source of information is Voorhoeve 1971; the data on hand is restricted to word lists.'

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1975. Languages of Irian Jaya: Checklist. Preliminary classification, language maps, wordlists (Pacific Linguistics B-31). Canberra: ANU.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C. L. 1971. Miscellaneous notes on languages in West Irian, New Guinea. In: Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 14 (Pacific Linguistics A-28), 47-114. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing for Towei. Sec. 2.6 'The Pauwasi Phylum' (p. 77): 'The only data on hand is the word lists collected by Galis (1956b). These are sufficient for purposes of provisional classification, but do not allow conclusions about phonological and grammatical structure.' (Stress statements elsewhere in the paper concern other languages, e.g. Sko, Morwap, not Pauwasi.)
sources.venue: Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 14 (Pacific Linguistics A-28)

sources.citation: Galis, Klaas Wilhelm. 1956 [issued 1957]. Etnologische survey van het Jafi-district (Onderafdeling Hollandia). Kantoor voor Bevolkingszaken, nota no. 102. Hollandia: Gouvernement van Nederlands Nieuw-Guinea. 1 v. (various pagings), maps; appendix 'Woordenlijst van enige talen (dialecten) van het Jafi-district, deels ontleend aan lijsten ten Kantore voor Bevolkingszaken'. Digitised by the National Library of Australia, nla.obj-52883617 (143 images).
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent or tone for any language. The only phonetic remarks concern Jafi proper (b~f, l~r, w~oe variation, endings -rep/-reb/-rup, prenasalised mb, nd). For Towei: speaker numbers, village list ('71. Towei 70'), tribal-boundary sketch map, and c. 12 pages of comparative wordlist in Dutch orthography (oe = u, dj, tj) with sporadic unexplained diacritics on some forms (e.g. Towei 'panà', 'edefí', 'těfoe', 'pěka'; Oeskoe 'osé', 'soró', 'klá') -- possibly accent, possibly vowel quality; no key is given anywhere in the report, so this is wordlist-only data, not a statement.
sources.venue: Etnologische survey van het Jafi-district (Onderafdeling Hollandia)

sources.citation: Wiktionary contributors. n.d. 'Appendix:Pauwasi word lists' (transcription of the comparative wordlist appendix of Galis, K. W. 1956, Ethnologische Survey van het Jafi-district: Jafi, Emoemoe, Dera, Monggowar, Waina, Doeboe, Towei, Molof, Oeskoe, Tofanma, Kaure columns). English Wiktionary.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Nothing: no transcription key and no word stress/accent/tone remark. 99 Towei forms, 17 with diacritics (acute: odofi 'blood', kaso 'snake', jemoe 'bird', and on monosyllables ge 'drink', mi 'louse', kon 'name', we 'fire', sam 'swim'; grave: poso 'day'; e-hacek = pepet/schwa: kema, peka, terenggi, kereser, keremolok, menderi, kerebana) -- the acute on monosyllables shows these marks are not a consistent stress notation. Useful only as a machine-readable copy of the Galis Towei list.

sources.citation: Pemerintah Kabupaten Keerom (developer credited on site). n.d. Portal Bahasa (Ibu) Keerom -- 'Mengenal, Melestarikan, dan Mewariskan Bahasa Ibu Keerom': district-by-district register of suku and kosakata for the 11 districts of Kab. Keerom, Papua; page 'Distrk Towe'.
sources.note: Nothing; empty shell. Recorded only as a local portal to re-check later for Towe vocabulary/audio (other Keerom districts on the site already carry tribe and vocabulary entries).

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. n.d. 'Tebi-Towe' (and stub page 'Towe'). Newguineaworld (DokuWiki hosted at Univ. Zurich),https://newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch/families/pauwasi-river/west-pauwasi-river/tebi-towe/start
sources.note: No prose statement on stress (historical phonology of consonants/vowels only, 'under construction'). Comparative tables recopy Wambaliau (2004) Towe Hitam survey forms with IPA stress marks (e.g. neˈme 'house', maˈmu 'breast', nemaˈrek 'child', tokoˈre 'yellow', sukuˈsi 'wallaby', keneˈmba 'machete' vs ˈpeja '3sg', ˈkaje 'sleep', ˈwafu 'ashes', furuˈkati 'fly'); my rough tally of the stress-marked polysyllables shows mostly final stress with a minority penult — raw second-hand data, not a published statement. The 'Towe' language page itself is an empty stub.
